title: Reusable SSTO/TSTO mass closure and LEO payload audit for OTA-TEC-0083
question: Source-grounded audit of the exact OTA-TEC-0083 document. Using primary, peer-reviewed and official launch-system sources, assess: (1) realistic Earth-surface-to-LEO delta-v including representative loss budgets; (2) chemical reusable SSTO feasibility and the structural/mass-fraction thresholds that distinguish SSTO from TSTO; (3) whether a reusable 100–150 t-to-400-km-LEO class is physically plausible as a 2030s/2040s descendant of current heavy reusable systems without validating any specific fictional design; (4) propellant choice trade-offs for methalox versus hydrolox in reusable first/upper-stage architectures; and (5) what mass-ratio, reserve, landing-propellant and engine-performance data would be required to close the fictional SSTO/TSTO hybrid. Identify wording that should be narrowed or reclassified. Do NOT evaluate or alter [F] ticket prices, operator names, 80–120 passenger count, 24–72 h turnaround, fictional schedules, Mars Credits, unlocks, journeys or other NOXIA balancing values.
why_now: OTA-TEC-0083 is now canonical and deliberately leaves the reusable SSTO mode [F/OFFEN]; a source-pinned engineering audit is needed before downstream NOXIA mappings harden.
real_world_anchor: Tsiolkovsky equation, reusable launch vehicle mass fractions, Starship-class TSTO architecture, chemical propulsion and LEO ascent performance.
novelty_reason: First source-pinned mass-closure audit of the canonical Starport-Launcher technical object.
validation_summary: Der Kandidat auditert die realwissenschaftlichen Anker von OTA-TEC-0083 (Starport-Launcher) und bestaetigt sie im Kern: Delta-v-Bedarf zu LEO, Massensensitivitaet der SSTO, TSTO als robuster Referenzmodus, Wiedereintritts-Herausforderung und die 100-150-t-Groessenordnung. Kein [R]-Anker wird widerlegt; die F/OFFEN-Markierungen (SSTO/TSTO-Hybrid, Propellantwahl, Abort) bleiben korrekt. Der Mehrwert liegt in quantitativen Praezisierungen (Aufstieg ~8,8-9,6 km/s inkl. Verluste, effektiver Missionswert ~9,5 km/s; Orbitalgeschwindigkeit bei 400 km 7,67 km/s statt ~7,8 km/s; Massenverhaeltnis ~8,8-9,5 hydrolox / ~16-17 methalox; zulaessiger Nicht-Treibstoff-Anteil eines SSTO inkl. Nutzlast <= ~6-11 % gegen reale Strukturkoeffizienten 0,04-0,13). Diese Schwellen treffen im Repository jedoch nicht primaer OTA-TEC-0083, sondern das kanonische Archivdokument OTA-SCI-0029-2025-DE (SSTO-Massenbudget des ASCE-Shuttles, dort als 'Reine Physik, keine Spekulation' und Hard-SF 9,8/10 gefuehrt): Dessen
